name: Which prompt is the spec?
note: A prompt is a specification, not a wish. Pick the request that carries your committed spec — versus the ones that outsource the decisions to the model's defaults.

items.prompt: Task: validate a US phone number. Which prompt gets you the right thing?
candidates: 'Validate a US phone number: 10 digits, optional +1 country code, allow spaces/dashes/parens as separators, reject everything else, return a bool; standard library only' — states format, edge handling, return type, and a constraint
'Write a phone number validator' — outsources every decision (which country? what format? what counts as valid?) to the model's defaults
'Write a really robust, production-grade phone validator' — adjectives, not a spec; 'robust' isn't a testable requirement
'Validate phone numbers using best practices' — defers the spec to an unstated standard
items.correct: 'Validate a US phone number: 10 digits, optional +1 country code, allow spaces/dashes/parens as separators, reject everything else, return a bool; standard library only' — states format, edge handling, return type, and a constraint
items.explanation: The precise prompt is your preregistered spec, handed to the AI. The others let the model pick an interpretation — often a reasonable one, rarely the one you actually meant.
items.principle: A good prompt states the spec; a bad one borrows the model's defaults.

items.prompt: Task: build a CLI that ingests a CSV, deduplicates it, and writes JSON. Best approach?
candidates: Decompose: prompt for the dedup function (with its preregistered invariant) first and verify it, then the I/O wrapper — you keep the architecture and verify each seam
One-shot the entire CLI in a single prompt and run it — the fastest path to 'done'
Prompt for the whole app plus tests plus docs in one giant request to save round-trips
Ask the AI to choose the architecture and implement everything without your input
items.correct: Decompose: prompt for the dedup function (with its preregistered invariant) first and verify it, then the I/O wrapper — you keep the architecture and verify each seam
items.explanation: Multi-part tasks reward decomposition: you own the seams (where bugs concentrate) and verify incrementally. One-shotting a multi-step task buries failures inside a wall of plausible code.
items.principle: One-shot the well-specified; decompose the moment architecture decisions appear.

items.prompt: The AI keeps adding a third-party dependency you don't want. Most effective fix?
candidates: Put it in the prompt as an explicit negative constraint: 'use only the standard library; do not add dependencies' — close the gap at the source
Delete the import each time it generates — fight the output instead of the prompt
Switch models and hope the next one doesn't add it
Accept the dependency; the AI usually knows best
items.correct: Put it in the prompt as an explicit negative constraint: 'use only the standard library; do not add dependencies' — close the gap at the source
items.explanation: The AI fills unstated gaps with common defaults (popular libraries). A negative constraint in the prompt closes the gap once; fixing the output by hand every time is rework you chose.
items.principle: Steer at the prompt, not the output — state the constraints you care about, including the negatives.
